statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Drosophila lines carrying a flamenco deletion, the retrotransposon ZAM is derepressed in somatic follicular cells and then invades the germline genome.
statements.evidence: This deletion leads to derepression of the retrotransposon ZAM in the somatic follicular cells and subsequent germline genome invasion.
statements.note: The abstract states that the flamenco deletion derepresses ZAM in follicular cells, after which ZAM invades the germline genome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Capture of ZAM by a germline piRNA cluster occurred frequently and early during isolation of the mutant line.
statements.evidence: Finally, we find that ZAM trapping in a germinal piRNA cluster is a frequent event that occurs early during the isolation of the mutant line.
statements.note: The abstract calls ZAM trapping in a germinal piRNA cluster a frequent event that occurs early in the isolation of the mutant line.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Trapping ZAM in a germline piRNA cluster restores fertility in females carrying the flamenco deletion.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that the germline can protect itself by trapping invading somatic-specific TEs into germline piRNA clusters.
statements.note: Protection is shown as ZAM silencing in germ cells; fertility is never measured, so the abstract neither supports nor refutes this.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The newly produced ZAM piRNAs derive from a fresh ZAM insertion into a germline dual-strand piRNA cluster and silence ZAM only in germ cells.
statements.evidence: These piRNAs originated from a new ZAM insertion into a germline dual-strand piRNA cluster and silence ZAM expression specifically in germ cells.
statements.note: The abstract traces the de novo ZAM piRNAs to a new insertion in a germline dual-strand cluster and says they silence ZAM specifically in germ cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Cytoplasmic Drosha isoforms are more abundant in cancer cell lines than in non-transformed human cells.
statements.evidence: In multiple cell lines, the endogenous mRNA expression of the Drosha isoforms correlates with the localization of endogenous Drosha proteins.
statements.note: Cell lines are compared only for isoform mRNA versus protein localization; no cancer versus non-transformed comparison is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The alternatively spliced Drosha transcripts, which have lost part of the arginine/serine-rich domain, are expressed in many kinds of human cells.
statements.evidence: In this study, we identify alternatively spliced Drosha transcripts that are devoid of a part of the arginine/serine-rich (RS-rich) domain and expressed in a large set of human cells.
statements.note: The abstract describes the spliced transcripts as devoid of part of the RS-rich domain and expressed in a large set of human cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two of the newly identified Drosha isoforms also occur in the cytoplasm, whereas the remaining two are found only in the nucleus.
statements.evidence: In contrast to their expected habitation, we find two isoforms also present in the cytoplasm, while the other two isoforms reside exclusively in the nucleus.
statements.note: The abstract reports two isoforms also present in the cytoplasm and two residing exclusively in the nucleus.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cells with cytoplasmic Drosha and cells without it did not differ significantly in how efficiently they processed pri-miRNAs.
statements.evidence: The pri-miRNA processing efficiency is not significantly different between groups of cells with or without cytoplasmic Drosha expression.
statements.note: The abstract states that pri-miRNA processing efficiency is not significantly different between the two groups of cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Time-course profiling of mature and primary miRNAs in Drosophila embryos uncovered shifts in which pri-miRNA isoforms are used.
statements.evidence: we profile a time course of mature and pri-miRNAs in Drosophila embryos and reveal the dynamics of miRNA production and degradation as well as dynamic changes in pri-miRNA isoform selection
statements.note: The abstract reports that the embryonic time course revealed dynamic changes in pri-miRNA isoform selection.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The identity of the 5' nucleotide of a mature miRNA affects how stable that miRNA is.
statements.evidence: We found that 5' nucleotides influence stability of mature miRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract states that 5' nucleotides influence the stability of mature miRNAs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Differences in half-life among mir-309 cluster miRNAs determine how their expression changes over time.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, distinct half-lives of miRNAs from the mir-309 cluster shape their temporal expression patterns
statements.note: The abstract says the distinct half-lives of mir-309 cluster miRNAs shape their temporal expression patterns.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mature miRNAs that begin with a uridine are more stable than those that begin with other nucleotides.
statements.evidence: We found that 5' nucleotides influence stability of mature miRNAs.
statements.note: The abstract says the 5' nucleotide influences stability but never says which nucleotide makes a miRNA more or less stable.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Flowering plants lacking histone H1 show developmental defects.
statements.evidence: Our results demonstrate that H1 enforces the separation of euchromatic and heterochromatic DNA methylation pathways by excluding the sRNA-generating branch of RdDM from non-CG-methylated heterochromatin.
statements.note: The abstract reports molecular effects of losing H1 on RdDM and sRNA production, not any plant phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Without histone H1, heterochromatic RdDM is enhanced, especially at the linker DNA between nucleosomes.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that loss of histone H1 enhances heterochromatic RdDM, preferentially at nucleosome linker DNA.
statements.note: The abstract states that loss of H1 enhances heterochromatic RdDM, preferentially at nucleosome linker DNA.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the absence of H1, small RNA production spreads quantitatively to loci that carry non-CG methylation.
statements.evidence: without H1 sRNA production quantitatively expands to non-CG-methylated loci
statements.note: The abstract reports that without H1, sRNA production quantitatively expands to non-CG-methylated loci.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Neither H3K9 methylation nor CG DNA methylation is needed for RdDM.
statements.evidence: Furthermore, H3K9me is dispensable for RdDM, as is CG DNA methylation.
statements.note: The abstract states that both H3K9me and CG DNA methylation are dispensable for RdDM.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mouse embryonic stem cells express pri-miR-124-1 even though they contain no mature miR-124.
statements.evidence: We find that primary (pri)-miR-124-1 is expressed in mouse embryonic stem cells where mature miR-124 is absent.
statements.note: The abstract reports pri-miR-124-1 expression in mouse embryonic stem cells in which mature miR-124 is absent.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: PTBP1 also blocks the processing of other neuron-specific miRNAs besides miR-124.
statements.evidence: This function for PTBP1 in repressing miR-124 biogenesis defines an additional regulatory loop in the already intricate interplay between these two molecules.
statements.note: Only miR-124 is examined; whether PTBP1 affects the biogenesis of other miRNAs is not addressed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mathematical modeling showed that the PTBP1-blocked pool of pri-miR-124 yields a robust, self-reinforcing switch in gene expression as PTBP1 falls during early neuronal differentiation.
statements.evidence: we find that the pool of pri-miR-124 whose maturation is blocked by PTBP1 creates a robust and self-reinforcing transition in gene expression as PTBP1 is depleted during early neuronal differentiation
statements.note: The modeling result is that the PTBP1-blocked pri-miR-124 pool creates a robust, self-reinforcing transition in gene expression as PTBP1 is depleted.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: By binding pri-miR-124-1 upstream of the stem-loop, PTBP1 suppresses mature miR-124 expression in vivo and DROSHA cleavage of the precursor in vitro.
statements.evidence: PTBP1 binds to this precursor RNA upstream of the miRNA stem-loop to inhibit mature miR-124 expression in vivo and DROSHA cleavage of pri-miR-124-1 in vitro.
statements.note: The abstract states that PTBP1 binds upstream of the stem-loop to inhibit mature miR-124 expression in vivo and DROSHA cleavage in vitro.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Even without encountering macrophages, rdrp1Δ and r3b2Δ mutants show a transcriptome already adapted to the stressful phagosomal environment.
statements.evidence: The transcriptomic profile of rdrp1Δ and r3b2Δ mutants revealed a pre-exposure adaptation to the stressful phagosomal environment even when the strains are not confronted by macrophages.
statements.note: The abstract reports a pre-exposure adaptation to the phagosomal environment in the mutants' transcriptomes even without macrophage contact.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mucor circinelloides mutants lacking RdRP1 or R3B2 cannot mount a proper virulence response to macrophage phagocytosis and have a lower virulence potential.
statements.evidence: Mutants in these genes are unable to launch a proper virulence response to macrophage phagocytosis, resulting in a decreased virulence potential.
statements.note: The abstract states that rdrp1 and r3b2 mutants fail to launch a proper virulence response and have decreased virulence potential.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: rdrp1Δ and r3b2Δ mutants grow more slowly than wild-type Mucor circinelloides under standard culture conditions.
statements.evidence: These results suggest that NCRIP represses key targets during regular growth and releases its control when a stressful environment challenges the fungus.
statements.note: NCRIP's regulatory role during regular growth is described, but no growth rate of the mutants is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When NCRIP is absent, the canonical RNAi machinery strongly represses centromeric retrotransposons.
statements.evidence: In the absence of NCRIP, these retrotransposons are robustly repressed by the canonical RNAi machinery
statements.note: The abstract states that without NCRIP the centromeric retrotransposons are robustly repressed by the canonical RNAi machinery.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Without PAB-1 and PAB-2, C. elegans loses both poly(A)-dependent and poly(A)-independent translational silencing.
statements.evidence: Depletion of PAB-1 and PAB-2 results in loss of both poly(A)-dependent and -independent translational silencing.
statements.note: The abstract states that depleting PAB-1 and PAB-2 causes loss of both poly(A)-dependent and -independent translational silencing.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: C. elegans PABPs are also required for miRNA-mediated silencing in adult worms.
statements.evidence: We find that C. elegans PABPs are required for miRNA-mediated silencing in embryonic and larval developmental stages, where they act through a multi-faceted mechanism.
statements.note: The requirement is reported for embryonic and larval stages only; adult worms are not mentioned either way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In C. elegans, PABPs make miRNA-mediated deadenylation proceed faster, although 3'UTR sequences can modulate this contribution.
statements.evidence: PABPs accelerate miRNA-mediated deadenylation, but this contribution can be modulated by 3'UTR sequences.
statements.note: The abstract states that PABPs accelerate miRNA-mediated deadenylation, with 3'UTR sequences able to modulate the effect.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deadenylation relies more heavily on PABP when the poly(A) tail lies farther away, but stronger miRNA-binding sites partly offset this dependence.
statements.evidence: While greater distances with the poly(A) tail exacerbate dependency on PABP for deadenylation, more potent miRNA-binding sites partially suppress this effect.
statements.note: The abstract states that greater distance to the poly(A) tail heightens PABP dependence for deadenylation and that more potent sites partially suppress this.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: pri-miR398c is made in the female gametophyte and is then moved into the ovule's sporophytic tissues, where it is processed.
statements.evidence: Moreover, pri-miR398c is transcribed in the female gametophyte but is then translocated to and processed in the ovule sporophytic tissues.
statements.note: The abstract states that pri-miR398c is transcribed in the female gametophyte, then translocated to and processed in the ovule sporophytic tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Together with ERECTA signaling, the SWR1 complex controls female gametophyte and integument growth in Arabidopsis thaliana by repressing MIR398c transcription early in megagametogenesis.
statements.evidence: chromatin-remodeling complex acts with the ERECTA receptor kinase-signaling pathway to control female gametophyte and integument growth in Arabidopsis thaliana by inhibiting transcription of the microRNA gene MIR398c in early-stage megagametogenesis
statements.note: The abstract states that SWR1 acts with ERECTA signaling to control gametophyte and integument growth by inhibiting MIR398c transcription early in megagametogenesis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the chalaza, AGO10 expression is activated jointly by SWR1 and ERECTA, and AGO10 traps miR398 so that three AGL genes stay expressed in the female gametophyte.
statements.evidence: Together, SWR1 and ERECTA also activate ARGONAUTE10 (AGO10) expression in the chalaza; AGO10 sequesters miR398, thereby ensuring the expression of three AGAMOUS-LIKE (AGL) genes (AGL51, AGL52, and AGL78) in the female gametophyte.
statements.note: The abstract states that SWR1 and ERECTA activate AGO10 in the chalaza and that AGO10 sequesters miR398 to ensure expression of three AGL genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The SWR1–ERECTA control of MIR398c also governs pollen development in Arabidopsis.
statements.evidence: In the context of sexual organ morphogenesis, these findings suggest that the spatiotemporal control of miRNA biogenesis, resulting from coordination between chromatin remodeling and cell signaling, is essential for proper ovule development in Arabidopsis.
statements.note: Only ovule (female) development is studied; the abstract says nothing about pollen or the male gametophyte.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: After HP1a germline knockdown, piRNAs targeting evolutionarily old transposons, which are concentrated in pericentric regions, decline significantly.
statements.evidence: Evolutionarily old transposons enriched in the pericentric regions exhibit significant loss in piRNAs targeting these transposons upon HP1a-GLKD.
statements.note: The abstract reports a significant loss of piRNAs targeting evolutionarily old, pericentric-enriched transposons upon HP1a-GLKD.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Total and Piwi-bound piRNAs mapping to clusters and transposon insertions are reduced after HP1a germline knockdown, mostly near telomeres and centromeres.
statements.evidence: HP1a germline knockdown (HP1a-GLKD) leads to a reduction in the total and Piwi-bound piRNAs mapping to clusters and transposons insertions, predominantly in the regions close to telomeres and centromeres
statements.note: The abstract states that HP1a-GLKD reduces total and Piwi-bound piRNAs from clusters and insertions, predominantly near telomeres and centromeres.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Germline knockdown of HP1a makes Drosophila females sterile.
statements.evidence: Our study suggests that HP1a functions to repress transposons in a chromosomal compartmentalised manner.
statements.note: Fertility is not assessed; the abstract reports only piRNA, splicing and transposon effects of HP1a-GLKD.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Germline knockdown of HP1a boosts splicing of transcripts from piRNA clusters in the telomere- and centromere-proximal regions.
statements.evidence: In addition, HP1a-GLKD increases the splicing of transcripts arising from clusters in above regions
statements.note: The abstract states that HP1a-GLKD increases splicing of transcripts arising from clusters in the regions near telomeres and centromeres.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Swapping the KRAB co-suppressor of ZFP266 for co-activator domains turns the protein from an inhibitor into a strong facilitator of iPSC reprogramming.
statements.evidence: Replacing the KRAB co-suppressor with co-activator domains converts ZFP266 from an inhibitor to a potent facilitator of iPSC reprogramming.
statements.note: The abstract states that replacing the KRAB co-suppressor with co-activator domains converts ZFP266 into a potent facilitator of reprogramming.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Depleting ZFP266 also enhances reprogramming of human cells into iPSCs.
statements.evidence: Of these, depletion of the predicted KRAB zinc finger protein (KRAB-ZFP) Zfp266 strongly and consistently enhances murine iPSC generation in several reprogramming settings, emerging as the most robust roadblock.
statements.note: The enhancement is reported for murine iPSC generation only; human cells are not examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen identified 24 genes that act as roadblocks to iPSC reprogramming.
statements.evidence: Here, we report 24 reprogramming roadblock genes identified by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome-wide knockout (KO) screening.
statements.note: The abstract reports 24 reprogramming roadblock genes found by a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Removing Zfp266 enhanced murine iPSC generation strongly and consistently across several reprogramming settings.
statements.evidence: Of these, depletion of the predicted KRAB zinc finger protein (KRAB-ZFP) Zfp266 strongly and consistently enhances murine iPSC generation in several reprogramming settings
statements.note: The abstract states that depleting Zfp266 strongly and consistently enhances murine iPSC generation in several reprogramming settings.
